subject.title: feat(gateway): restrict session tools by authenticated hosting node

question: After the cron-cap and metadata defects are fixed, should OpenClaw accept `gateway.tools.byNode` as a permanent public fail-closed tool-authorization boundary keyed by authenticated node identity?
rationale: The code defects are mechanical, but making this config a supported security boundary and accepting zero-tool fail-closed behavior is a product/security ownership decision.

options.title: Fix, rebase, then review boundary
options.body: Repair the cron and metadata blockers, refresh against current main, and then have a gateway/security owner explicitly accept or reject the public boundary.

options.title: Pause public config
options.body: Keep the PR open or close it until the browser/node routing design proves this public config surface is still needed.

options.title: Narrow to internal plumbing
options.body: Split out only reusable authenticated-node threading and defer the operator-facing `gateway.tools.byNode` config until a later approved design.

recommendation.title: Fix, rebase, then review boundary
recommendation.body: Repair the cron and metadata blockers, refresh against current main, and then have a gateway/security owner explicitly accept or reject the public boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans gateway security posture and the adjacent browser relay direction that recently landed.
